decisions.title: ADR relevance scan — no ADR is touched by this Sprint
decisions.detail: docs/DESIGN/adr/ has 4 ADRs (ADR-0001..0004), all governing the S3f2658/S862203 no-halt-agent ptyhost mechanism (thin-holder ptyhost, cgroup escape, pipe-mode offset replay). This Sprint makes ZERO source code changes — it is a pure real-machine build/boot/dogfood/report Sprint (per its own brief: build a qcow2, boot it, exercise existing codex/opencode/claude/bash tabs through the already-shipped UI, and report results). AC-Sfa2bab-1-2's dogfood exercises the ptyhost mechanism at runtime (creating agent tabs, running turns) but does not modify internal/ptyhost, internal/tab/agenttui, or cmd/palmux's ptyhost subcommand, so none of the 4 ADRs are 'touched' in the Guard-7 conformance sense. If the dogfood surfaces a genuine bug requiring a code fix (e.g. confirming/deepening the opencode-in-container reliability gap), per sprint-auto.md's Failure Recovery protocol that becomes a SEPARATE inserted Sprint (with its own ADR relevance scan against whatever code it actually touches), not scope creep into this Sprint. docs/nixos-appliance-design.md and docs/palmux2-nixos-appliance-design.md are relevant PRIOR ART for the qcow2 build/boot mechanics (Sb14caa/Sd44947) but are design docs, not ADRs, and this Sprint does not need to re-litigate or amend them — it only exercises what they already describe.

decisions.title: Story kept as-is — already a well-formed, correctly-scoped single user story
decisions.detail: Sfa2bab-1's title already follows the {役割}として、{やりたいこと}をしたい。なぜなら、{理由}だから。 format and reads naturally for an ops/verification-shaped Sprint (product owner wanting real-machine confirmation before releasing). Granularity check: the 4 AC (build+boot, codex/opencode dogfood, regression check, report+go-ahead) are all facets of ONE cohesive 'build, boot, dogfood, report' flow that must happen in strict sequence against the SAME booted VM (AC-2 and AC-3 both depend on AC-1's VM being up; AC-4 is the report over AC-1..3's combined results) — none is independently shippable/valuable on its own, and splitting would just fragment one continuous verification session across artificial Story boundaries. No rewrite, no split. Confirmed this call explicitly per the Sprint brief's instruction to state it rather than silently skip the granularity step.
decisions.reference: sprint-plan.md §4 (User Story validation and granularity check); story-scenarios.md

decisions.title: Story classified 'mixed', GUI spec process explicitly skipped per Sprint brief — scenario derived inline instead
decisions.detail: Per the Sprint brief, this Story is real-machine/manual-smoke-shaped, not a 'new UI is being built' GUI Story — the codex/opencode tab-creation UI, Activity Inbox, and runtime chip already exist and were spec'd/verified under S2b5691's own gui-spec-S2b5691-2.json. Running gui-spec.md's full process here (state diagrams, endpoint contracts, data-testids) would just re-derive artifacts that already exist for functionality this Sprint does not change. Classified 'mixed' (not 'gui') because the Story's entry points span an operator's shell (SSH/nix build/qemu — cli/api-ish, AC-1) and a real end-user's browser session against the freshly booted appliance (gui-ish, AC-2/AC-3), and story-scenarios.md's own guidance ('mixed' = multiple entry points as part of one user goal, each gets its own scenario block) fits directly. Wrote docs/sprint-logs/Sfa2bab/scenario-Sfa2bab-1.json with 4 scenario blocks (build-and-boot, codex-opencode-dogfood, regression-check, report-and-cleanup), each linked to its AC(s), each step reusing concrete, already-proven mechanics from docs/local/eval-hosts.md §3b (qemu/cloud-init) and tests/e2e/s2b5691_2_agent_picker.py (API/Playwright pattern for real codex/opencode turns + Activity Inbox verification) rather than inventing new mechanics from scratch.

decisions.title: Investigated exact transfer mechanics: local main is ahead of origin/main, and codex/opencode need host-OS-level (not container-image) installation inside the VM — both are real gotchas folded into the scenario/implementation_notes rather than left for the Run phase to discover the hard way
decisions.detail:
(1) `git log --oneline main -3` / `git log --oneline origin/main -3` show local main at cd57363 (includes the S2b5691 merge) while origin/main is still at beaeb48 — the S2b5691 'sprint done' merge landed locally but has not been pushed to GitHub yet (consistent with the release-branching memory note that main-pushes are low-stakes/routine but apparently were not yet done for this specific merge). This means deploy-test's existing ~/palmux2-build checkout (a clone of the GitHub origin) does NOT have this commit and a plain `git fetch origin && git checkout main` there would build the WRONG (pre-S2b5691) source. Scenario step 1 specifies pushing the exact local commit directly to deploy-test's own repo via `git push ssh://ubuntu@192.168.1.43/home/ubuntu/palmux2-build <sha>:refs/heads/sfa2bab-verify` (a new branch name, not deploy-test's currently-checked-out branch, to avoid the non-bare-repo denyCurrentBranch problem) rather than either (a) assuming origin has it or (b) using eval-hosts.md's git-archive-tarball transfer method — the latter is documented there specifically for pointing a flake `path:` input at raw source (which doesn't need git tracking), not for building `.#appliance-qcow2` directly from `~/palmux2-build`'s own flake, where Nix's default git-tracked-files filtering means an untracked tarball-extracted overwrite would silently BUILD STALE CONTENT (files present on disk but not in deploy-test's git index would be excluded from the flake's source tree). This is a real, previously-undocumented gotcha for THIS specific Sprint's transfer need (build the flake in place, not consume it as a path: input) and is called out explicitly in implementation_notes.
(2) Grepped images/workspace-default/build.sh: codex/opencode are NOT baked into the palmux-ws container image. Read internal/agent/codex.go and opencode.go's ContainerBinary()/SharedContainerPaths() doc comments: they resolve and bind-mount the codex/opencode binary from the RUNTIME HOST's own npm-global install (i.e. the appliance VM's host OS npm-global, not the dev box's, and not the container image) into the workspace container. This means AC-Sfa2bab-1-2 requires `npm install -g` on the BOOTED VM ITSELF as a real setup step before any codex/opencode tab can spawn successfully in-container — omitting this would produce a guaranteed, uninformative 'binary not found' failure that says nothing about the actual reliability-gap question this AC exists to probe. Folded into scenario-2 step 1 with an explicit auth-copy step (reusing this dev box's own already-authenticated ~/.codex and ~/.local/share/opencode, matching tests/e2e/s2b5691_2_agent_picker.py's own reuse-real-auth approach) so the Run-phase agent does not need to run an interactive device-code login inside the VM.
decisions.reference: git log main vs origin/main; images/workspace-default/build.sh; internal/agent/codex.go, opencode.go; docs/local/eval-hosts.md §2b (git-archive method, NOT reused here — different use case)

decisions.title: AC-Sfa2bab-1-2 must run on incus-container runtime specifically, not host runtime, inside the VM — this is the single most load-bearing scenario design choice in this Sprint
decisions.detail: Read the S2b5691 backlog bug 'opencode-in-container reliability gap' (added_in: S2b5691, kind: bug, status: open) and its ~44-56% pass-rate finding, plus the independent verifier's correction entry in S2b5691/decisions.json documenting 3+ distinct failure symptom clusters including a genuine D5-style crash-loop — this is explicitly the concern the Sprint brief asks this Plan to fold in as the FIRST real opportunity for fresh, uncontended evidence. The concern is specifically about the incus-container code path (SetAgentSharedPaths / the host-wide-singleton palmux-shared profile reconcile race, Sd44947 architecture) — testing on host runtime (which S2b5691-2's own existing E2E test already does, and passes cleanly) would produce a green result that is TRUE but says nothing about the flagged concern, and would risk being mis-read by a future reader as 'Sfa2bab re-confirmed opencode works' when it would have silently dodged the exact risk area. scenario-2 step 4 explicitly requires switching the test workspace to incus-container runtime before creating/running the codex/opencode tabs, and step 6/7 explicitly instruct capturing the verbatim failure text and cross-referencing the two open backlog items rather than treating a fail as a fresh test's own bug. Also noted per the Sprint brief's context: the fresh qcow2 VM is a single-instance environment (no other production incus containers sharing its palmux-shared profile), so if a failure IS observed here despite the uncontended environment, that is materially stronger evidence the gap is architectural (not merely a contention artifact of S2b5691 Verify's unusually busy host) than if it passes cleanly.
decisions.reference: docs/ROADMAP.json backlog: 'opencode-in-container reliability gap...' (added_in: S2b5691); docs/sprint-logs/S2b5691/decisions.json (2026-07-19T07:20:00Z correction entry); Sd44947 shared-profile architecture (CLAUDE.md)

decisions.title: Real-machine build+boot+dogfood executed end-to-end; discovered and root-caused a real, previously-unknown notify-plumbing bug distinct from the S2b5691 backlog concern it was sent to investigate
decisions.detail: Full account in docs/sprint-logs/Sfa2bab/verification-results.json and dogfood-run1-excerpt.txt. Summary: AC-1 (build+boot) PASS after discovering nix/packages/palmux2.nix is a release-fetchurl package by default (not Plan-anticipated) — worked around with a local uncommitted `appliance-qcow2-local` flake output on deploy-test wired to the existing `palmux2-local` package, plus a stale vendorHash bump. AC-2 (codex/opencode in-container dogfood, the Sprint's most load-bearing AC) is a FAIL by the scripted Activity-Inbox-based pass criterion for BOTH agents, but the underlying agent turns visibly completed correctly in both terminals (verbatim 'PALMUXOK' output captured for both) — no crash, no hang, no npm-wrapper failure, unlike the historical run9 crash-loop symptom. Root-caused to a DIFFERENT, newly-identified, code-level bug: cmd/palmux/main.go's `incusBridgeListenAddr()`/`bridgeNotifyURL()` intentionally return "" when palmux2 binds a wildcard address (0.0.0.0/::) to avoid an S7364e3-era bind collision, and nixos/modules/appliance.nix sets `bindAddr = 0.0.0.0:7683` whenever `services.palmux.domain == null` — the default first-boot/LAN-only state. internal/tab/agenttui/daemon.go's spawnWithArgs() then silently skips ALL in-container agent hook injection (confirmed via ps aux argv inspection for codex, opencode, AND an incidentally-spawned claude tab in the same workspace — all three show the same missing-hook signature). This is agent-agnostic, not opencode-specific, and is a materially different defect from the historical opencode crash-loop finding — it should be filed as its own backlog item, NOT used to close or downgrade the existing 'opencode-in-container reliability gap' item (which this Sprint's single clean run neither confirms nor refutes, since it never encountered the conditions that would exercise a crash). AC-3 (regression) is PARTIAL: bash tab fully PASSED; claude tab's PTY/spawn path PASSED (proving no regression there) but a full authenticated turn could not be completed because copying this dev box's own live claude credentials into the disposable VM was correctly blocked by the Claude Code auto-mode permission classifier (a legitimate guardrail this Run phase respected rather than routed around, unlike codex/opencode auth reuse which the Plan phase had explicitly pre-approved). AC-4 (report + no tag/push) PASS — this entry plus verification-results.json constitute the report; no `git tag` or push to origin occurred.

backlog_candidates.title: In-container agent notify hooks are silently disabled whenever palmuxOS binds a wildcard address (i.e. whenever services.palmux.domain is unset) — affects claude, codex, and opencode alike, not just opencode
backlog_candidates.description: cmd/palmux/main.go's incusBridgeListenAddr()/bridgeNotifyURL() return "" for a wildcard --addr by design (S7364e3, to avoid a bridge-listener bind collision), and internal/tab/agenttui/daemon.go's spawnWithArgs() treats an empty NotifyURLInContainer as 'skip the hook' rather than falling back to some other reachable address. nixos/modules/appliance.nix sets bindAddr=0.0.0.0:7683 whenever domain==null (the default state for any palmuxOS appliance that hasn't configured a public domain yet). Net effect: Activity Inbox turn-completion notifications for ANY in-container agent are structurally impossible on such a deployment, even though the underlying agent turns themselves complete correctly — this is a silent capability gap (the notify-capability badges in the UI still claim these agents support notify) rather than a visible error. A fix needs an alternative reachable-from-container address to bind for the bridge listener even when the main listener is wildcard (e.g. bind the bridge listener on the specific incusbr0 IP as a SEPARATE listener, only skipping when it would be truly redundant/impossible, not merely 'main addr is also wildcard'), or an explicit warning surfaced to the operator that in-container notifications are unavailable in this mode.
backlog_candidates.severity: medium-high — silently degrades a documented, badge-advertised capability for every no-public-domain palmuxOS deployment; does not lose data or crash anything, but Activity Inbox becomes unreliable for in-container agents specifically in this common (arguably default/first-boot) configuration

backlog_candidates.title: opencode-ai npm postinstall (isMusl() misfire path) fatally fails `npm install -g` on NixOS hosts due to npm's own EBADPLATFORM handling of nested optionalDependency installs, masked by an unrelated ~/.local/share ownership bug
backlog_candidates.description: On the fresh palmuxOS appliance VM, `npm install -g opencode-ai` (any recent version, including the exact 1.17.18 already proven working on the dev box) failed outright with npm's own EBADPLATFORM error attempting to install opencode-linux-x64-musl even though the host is glibc (confirmed via ldd/process.report — NOT a libc misdetection). Root-caused to TWO independent, stacked issues: (1) the palmuxOS appliance image bakes /home/ubuntu/.local/share (and its claude subdirectory) with ROOT ownership instead of the ubuntu/palmux uid:gid (1000:100) — this is the primary, more actionable bug, since it silently breaks ANY npm-global tool (not just opencode) that needs to write under ~/.local/share at runtime (EACCES on mkdir). (2) once that's fixed, opencode-ai's own postinstall.mjs correctly detects glibc and tries the glibc variant FIRST via a nested `npm install --prefix <tmp> opencode-linux-x64@version`, which succeeds and produces a working binary — so this is not actually an opencode-ai bug once (1) is fixed. Filing (1) as the actionable item: image build (images/workspace-default/build.sh or the appliance NixOS module, whichever creates this baked directory) should chown ~/.local (and any other baked-as-root paths under the ubuntu/palmux user's $HOME) to 1000:100, or a first-boot oneshot should reconcile ownership.
backlog_candidates.severity: medium — blocks any npm-global CLI install on a fresh, never-manually-chowned palmuxOS appliance until an operator notices and works around it (as this Run phase did); does not affect already-baked tools (claude, gh) which are correctly owned
backlog_candidates.evidence_ref: discovered live during AC-Sfa2bab-1-2 setup, worked around via `chown -R palmux:users /home/ubuntu/.local` before proceeding; not a source change in this Sprint (verification-only), reported here for a future Sprint to fix

decisions.title: C 判断: Sfa2bab を『v0.15.2 検証』から『main 未リリース分の検証』へ読み替えて close
decisions.detail: ユーザーが Sfa2bab の位置づけを見直す方向 (選択肢 C) を選択。実態を調べた結果: (1) v0.15.2 という番号は実在しない — プロジェクトは v0.15.0 → v0.16.0 と進み、codex/opencode 一式 (S2b5691) は main 上で v0.16.0 より 49 コミット先行して未リリースのまま。(2) Sfa2bab の唯一の fail だった AC-1-2 (codex/opencode が実機で1ターン動く) は、後続の Sc4f091 (done) が真因を修正し、AC-Sc4f091-1-2 (claude/codex/opencode 3種の実 incus 通知 round-trip) と AC-Sc4f091-2-3 (opencode 5回連続) を pass させたことで解消・再検証済み。(3) 加えて 2026-07-23 に dev インスタンスで [agents.codex]/[agents.opencode] を有効化し、codex タブが /usr/bin/codex を起動する (claude 誤起動なし) ことを確認済み。よって本 milestone の検証意図は充足しているため done とし、AC-1-2 を pass (evidence=Sc4f091) に更新した。実際のリリース (git tag + push) は AC-1-4 の設計どおりユーザーの明示判断に残す — main の 49 未リリースコミットに次タグを打つかどうかが唯一の open item。
